companies.name: Amazon
companies.context: Net profits surged 39% and revenue rose in Q3; beat on top line, bottom line, and AWS revenue after being seen as lagging other hyperscalers on AI narrative.

companies.name: AWS
companies.context: Beat revenue expectations in Q3, helping Amazon rejoin the AI growth narrative after previously lagging peers.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.context: Posted a topline and earnings beat but stock traded down 3-4% after hours before recovering; praised for model-agnostic AI strategy and Copilot integration with Excel.

companies.name: Meta
companies.context: Topline beat but roughly $12 billion earnings miss attributed to a one-time tax charge related to the Big Beautiful Bill Act; stock reacted negatively with skepticism around Zuckerberg's capital allocation.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.context: Beat on revenue but missed on earnings; stock down ~4% after hours. Robotaxi fleet seen as 1-2 years behind Waymo, but bulls cite superior cost structure and data flywheel.

companies.name: Apple
companies.context: Beat on top and bottom line but China sales continue to decline year over year and iPhone revenue nearly missed; trading at 40x PE with very low growth seen as steep.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.context: Described as top of the world with core AI factory build-out going flawlessly; skepticism raised about expansion into data centers in space, humanoids, and quantum computing.

companies.name: Alphabet
companies.context: Up 247% over five years; Gemini models cited as serving 150 enterprises processing 1 trillion tokens each, though critics noted this implies only ~$150M in annual revenue, roughly 0.3% of GCP revenue.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.context: Microsoft reportedly revealed OpenAI lost $11.5 billion last quarter; API processing ~250 trillion tokens per month. Losses characterized as CAPEX investments rather than operating losses.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.context: Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX will build data centers in orbit; described as having structural monopoly-like advantages in space versus Tesla's brutally competitive automotive market.

companies.name: Waymo
companies.context: Referenced as being 1-2 years ahead of Tesla's Robotaxi fleet currently; used as benchmark for autonomous vehicle deployment.

companies.name: Coinbase
companies.context: During earnings call, Brian Armstrong deliberately read off words from a prediction market created around his speech, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, blockchain, staking, and Web3.

companies.name: Palantir
companies.context: Filed suit against two former employees accused of stealing confidential data to build rival AI firm Percepta; described as one of the worst companies to steal from.

companies.name: Percepta
companies.context: Rival AI firm allegedly founded by former Palantir employees using stolen confidential data; backed by General Catalyst.

companies.name: General Catalyst
companies.context: Backed Percepta, the AI startup founded by former Palantir employees now being sued for theft of trade secrets.

companies.name: BlackRock
companies.context: Reported to have been stung by loans to businesses accused of breathtaking fraud through private credit funds.

companies.name: 1X
companies.context: Mentioned as a humanoid robotics benchmark; Tesla's full self-driving approach to humanoids described as potentially years behind 1X.

companies.name: Slack
companies.context: Cited as an analogy for Microsoft products — a superior product that dominated workplace chat despite competitive pressure.

companies.name: Toyota
companies.context: Briefly mentioned in context of an internationally sold truck priced at $10-20K that may be blocked for import into the US.

people.name: Andy Jassy
people.context: Previously on the defensive about Amazon's AI narrative; now 'back on the offensive' after strong Q3 earnings beat across all metrics.

people.name: Satya Nadella
people.context: Credited with positioning Microsoft well for AI opportunities, described as having received more recognition for AI potential than Amazon or Google.

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.context: Compared to Bezos in terms of contrarian capital allocation; VR/Metaverse spend criticized as not yet ROI positive while Reels success praised.

people.name: Jeff Bezos
people.context: Referenced as a parallel to Zuckerberg — once seen as crazy for building AWS, ultimately vindicated.

people.name: Elon Musk
people.context: Discussed plans for data centers in orbit via SpaceX; Tesla's full self-driving approach to humanoid robots described as a 'full moon shot' strategy.

people.name: Jensen Huang
people.context: Described as 'the most value creative founder-CEO in human history' having created $5 trillion in value; his relaxed demeanor in Korea cited as a positive signal.

people.name: Brian Armstrong
people.context: Deliberately read aloud every word from a prediction market about his earnings call, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, blockchain, staking, and Web3.

people.name: Xi Jinping
people.context: Met with Trump, leading to US agreeing to lower fentanyl-related tariffs on Chinese goods from 20% to 10% and China easing rare earth export controls for one year.

people.name: Marc Andreessen
people.context: Referenced as a Halloween costume worn by host Jordi.

people.name: Sam Altman
people.context: Referenced as a Halloween costume worn by host Tyler, dressed as 'Sam Altman at 2008 WWDC.'

people.name: Ilya Sutskever
people.context: Referenced as a Halloween costume; humorous claim made that 'AGI has been achieved.'

topics.name: Mag 7 Q3 2025 Earnings Recap
topics.summary: Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Tesla, Apple, NVIDIA, and Alphabet all reported earnings; Amazon and Microsoft were strong, Meta had a surprise earnings miss on a tax charge, Tesla missed on earnings, Apple beat but faces China headwinds.

topics.name: US-China Trade and Tariffs
topics.summary: Trump lowered fentanyl-related tariffs on Chinese goods from 20% to 10% after meeting with Xi Jinping; China agreed to ease rare earth export controls for one year.

topics.name: AI Spending and Enterprise Adoption
topics.summary: Debate over whether AI enterprise revenue is meaningful; Gemini's 150-enterprise/1-trillion-token stat criticized as implying only ~$150M in revenue or 0.3% of GCP; AI broadly not considered a bubble.

topics.name: OpenAI Financial Losses
topics.summary: Microsoft data revealed OpenAI lost $11.5 billion last quarter; hosts debated whether these are true losses or CAPEX investments given massive infrastructure build-out.

topics.name: Tesla Robotaxi vs. Waymo
topics.summary: Tesla's Robotaxi seen as 1-2 years behind Waymo currently, but Tesla bulls argue superior cost structure, manufacturing scale, and data flywheel could enable a comeback.

topics.name: Data Centers in Space
topics.summary: Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX plans to put data centers in orbit; NVIDIA also pushing this concept, though hosts questioned whether it was genuine or forward-looking marketing.

topics.name: Meta Metaverse ROI
topics.summary: Zuckerberg's all-in bet on VR/Metaverse remains unproven with no signs of ROI; Reels at $50B run rate praised as a counter-balance.

topics.name: Apple China Decline
topics.summary: Apple's China revenue continues to decline year over year; stock trading at 40x PE with very low growth seen as stretched despite no immediate AI threat.

topics.name: Palantir Trade Secret Lawsuit
topics.summary: Palantir sued two former employees for allegedly stealing confidential data to build rival AI startup Percepta, backed by General Catalyst.

topics.name: Prediction Markets on Earnings Calls
topics.summary: Coinbase's Brian Armstrong acknowledged a prediction market tracking words he'd say on his earnings call and deliberately read off every missed word at the end of the call.

topics.name: Private Credit and Fraud Risk
topics.summary: BlackRock reported losses from loans to businesses accused of fraud via private credit funds; hosts noted large-scale fraud tends to appear during good economic times.

topics.name: Humanoid Robots
topics.summary: Tesla's approach to humanoid robots criticized as potentially years behind 1X if it bypasses teleoperation; broader bullishness on the space category.

key_claims: Amazon net profits surged 39% in Q3 2025, beating on top line, bottom line, and AWS revenue.
Microsoft stock fell 3-4% after hours despite an earnings and revenue beat.
Meta's ~$12 billion earnings miss was attributed to a one-time tax charge related to the 'Big Beautiful Bill Act.'
Meta's Reels is now a $50 billion annual revenue run-rate business.
Tesla's Robotaxi fleet is 'a year or two behind Waymo's right now.'
Apple is trading at 40x PE with very low growth.
Alphabet's Gemini serving 150 enterprises at 1 trillion tokens each implies only ~$150M in revenue, roughly 0.3% of GCP annual revenue.
OpenAI lost $11.5 billion last quarter per data revealed through Microsoft.
OpenAI's API is processing approximately 250 trillion tokens per month.
Jensen Huang described as 'the most value creative founder-CEO in human history' having created $5 trillion in value.
SpaceX will build data centers in orbit.
Amazon is still only up 62% over five years versus Alphabet's 247%.
US agreed to lower fentanyl-related tariffs on Chinese goods from 20% to 10%; China will ease rare earth export controls for one year.
Palantir alleges former employees stole confidential data to build rival AI firm Percepta, backed by General Catalyst.
Tesla's full self-driving approach to humanoid robots could be 'years behind' 1X if it goes straight to full autonomy without teleoperation.
